item.title: Yemen Says It’s Retaken Mocha as Battle for Bab El-Mandeb Looms
item.description: Yemen’s armed forces wrested control of the Red Sea city of Mocha on Monday after battles with the Iran-backed Houthis, according to state-run Saba, which puts the internationally recognized government closer to taking over the vital Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
item.dc:creator: list.metadata.agency
item.content:encoded: (Bloomberg) -- Yemen’s armed forces wrested control of the Red Sea city of Mocha on Monday after battles with the Iran-backed Houthis, according to state-run Saba, which puts the internationally recognized government closer to taking over the vital Bab el-Mandeb Strait.The Yemeni forces, backed by a Saudi-led coalition, have snatched back the port city from the Houthi group one day after announcing a full-scale military campaign to recapture all territory held by the militia. The Houthis had controlled Mocha since early September as they embarked on a military campaign against Saudi Arabia in recent months, ending a 2022 ceasefire. The city is located about 180 kilometers (112 miles) south of Hodeida, another stronghold of the militant group.Seizing Mocha helped the Houthis tighten control on Bab el-Mandeb, a narrow chokepoint between the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden that Saudi Arabia had been using to export oil and bypass the Strait of Hormuz, which has become a battlefield in the US-Iran war.Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan on Monday agreed to the immediate “implementation of the collective defense commitments” during an emergency meeting of their defense alliance in Riyadh. The three countries, which signed a defense pact in August, will ensure the provision of “military forces and capabilities and ensure their rapid deployment in the Kingdom,” according to a joint statement. The meeting reaffirmed “solidarity in confronting the heinous attacks against the Kingdom and the holy sites,” Saudi Defense Minister Khalid bin Salman said in a posting on X. The Houthis recently attacked Saudi Arabia’s Madinah, one of Islam’s holiest cities, the Saudi-led coalition said in early October.The coalition said it’s providing air support for Yemeni ground forces during the ongoing operation, with 100 fighter jets participating in the military campaign early Monday. Its air forces also protect Bab el-Mandeb, the coalition said.The Houthi escalation against Saudi Arabia in recent months resulted in damage to energy infrastructure and tankers. The group said it stepped up attacks as its cities and ports are under “siege” from the Saudi government.Yemen’s government forces also started an offensive on Sanaa Monday, according to its military spokesperson. The Yemeni forces have repeatedly struck the capital, which the Houthis have controlled since 2014, over the past days.Saudi Arabia “reiterates its full political and military support for the Presidential Leadership Council,” headed by Rashad Al-Alimi, “to end the coup and retake the state and its institutions from the Houthi militia,” the kingdom’s Foreign Ministry said.More stories like this are available on bloomberg.com©2026 Bloomberg L.P.

item.title: Omani pilot used crash axe to stab Captain Smit Machchar during Flydubai flight —what is its purpose? Expert explains
item.description: A Flydubai co-pilot allegedly attacked Captain Smit Machchhar with a cockpit crash axe and attempted to take control of flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv. The aircraft later diverted to Saudi Arabia. What is the purpose of crash axe in cockpit? Aviation expert explains.
item.dc:creator: Garvit Bhirani
item.content:encoded: Flydubai co-pilot Hamam al-Hammami, an Omani national, allegedly “attempted to carry out a terrorist act” during Wednesday’s flight FZ1073 to Israel's Tel Aviv. He used a crash axe from the cockpit to attack Indian Captain Smit Machchhar, according to the UAE state news agency WAM, citing Attorney General Counsellor Hamad Saif al-Shamsi. Aviation expert Harsh Vardhan told LiveMint that the cockpit carries several safety items, including a crash axe, portable fire extinguisher, flashlights, life vests and fireproof gloves. He explained that the crash axe can be used when crew members need to access areas behind aircraft panels during a fire or when access to a door becomes difficult because of an electrical-system failure or a jammed door. "In cockpit various safety equipments like Crash Axe, Portable fire extinguisher, Flash Lights, Life vests, Fire proof gloves etc are kept. Usage of these items during emergency varies. Crash Axe is used to open the panel in case of fire in case the electrical system to open door fails or doors are jammed for some reason," Vardhan stated.What happened to Flight FZ1073?The incident occurred roughly two-and-a-half hours after the Dubai-Tel Aviv flight departed on September 30. Reuters reported that the aircraft plunged about 16,000 feet in around 30 seconds after the cockpit confrontation. The autopilot disconnected and the Boeing 737 MAX 8 accelerated during the descent before the situation was brought under control.Machchhar survived the attack and was subsequently treated for his injuries. A reserve pilot on board took control of the aircraft and landed it safely in Saudi Arabia, while the co-pilot was detained and later transferred to UAE custody.Co-pilot allegedly planned attack before joining flydubaiThe flydubai co-pilot who allegedly stabbed his captain in an attempt to take control of the aircraft had told UAE investigators that he had planned the attack before joining the Dubai government-owned airline, according to Reuters citing two Israeli officials familiar with the investigation.A third source briefed on the UAE probe said the Omani national had allegedly intended to crash last Wednesday’s flight into Ben-Gurion Airport near Tel Aviv. The co-pilot had also flown a Tel Aviv-bound flight earlier this year and allegedly considered hijacking and crashing that aircraft but ultimately abandoned the plan, the source said.The reason for his decision to drop the earlier plan was not immediately known. However, the source said the co-pilot was believed to have known someone who was travelling on that flight.The sources spoke anonymously because they were discussing an ongoing investigation. UAE and Israeli authorities had not immediately responded to Reuters' requests for comment, while flydubai also did not immediately comment.Australia probes co-pilot’s links to countryAustralian authorities are examining the flydubai co-pilot’s connections to the country after he allegedly stabbed his captain and attempted to take control of flight FZ1073, a police spokesperson said on Sunday.The Victorian Joint Counter Terrorism Team, comprising the Australian Federal Police, Victoria Police and the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation (ASIO), was "investigating the man's links to Australia," the Australian Federal Police spokesperson said.
